key_insight: ClinicalBERT shows demographic bias amplification in its language predictions, especially for race and gender associations, rather than simply reflecting training-corpus frequencies.
clinical_relevance: This matters because biased clinical language models could distort decision-support outputs and reinforce inequities if used in high-stakes workflows.
method: Audited ClinicalBERT with Log Probability Bias Analysis (LPBA) across demographic descriptors and semantic categories.
Probed masked language model behavior on 98 real clinical sentence templates spanning eight race-gender combinations.
Compared model outputs against MIMIC-III corpus term frequencies to separate data disparity from model amplification.
evidence_signal: Among 32 statistically significant findings, 65.6% contradicted corpus distributions, with stronger mismatch for Black patients (80%) and agency attribution under MLM probing (87.5%).
watch_item: Because the study uses one pretrained model and template-based probing, results should not be assumed to generalize to all clinical NLP systems or real-world deployment settings.
paper_title: A Computational Audit of Demographic Association Encoding in ClinicalBERT Language Predictions
